predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Rhodesia row (1967-1978) draws the same 392,765 km2 shape.

land.text: 'On 18 April 1980, Zimbabwe Rhodesia became the independent Republic of Zimbabwe within the Commonwealth of Nations'

successors.note: Between 11-12 December 1979 and 18 April 1980 the land was Southern Rhodesia under British rule (a governor and British-supervised transition); Cliopatria's Republic of Zimbabwe row begins in 1983, so its 1980-1982 years are carried by this row's shape.

capitals.name: Salisbury (Harare)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Salisbury'; the city is now Harare.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but for 1979 only: the state 'existed from 1 June 1979' and on 11 December 1979 'shall cease to be an independent State and become part of Her Majesty's dominions'; 1980-1982 belong to the Republic of Zimbabwe, independent on 18 April 1980

keyframe_review.note: Years only. Cliopatria draws this shape for 1979-1982; the page's infobox spans 1 June 1979 to 18 April 1980, but its own quotation of the law ends the independent state on 11 December 1979 (the name reverted to Southern Rhodesia at the Lancaster House Agreement of 21 December 1979). The infobox gives no area, so the 392,765 km2 cannot be compared on this page; the gazetteer shows 1,309 cells against 1,304 for the country of Zimbabwe, with 33 cells over Botswana and Zambia and 28 Zimbabwean cells missing, a border-precision difference.

region.text: the territory of the Republic of Rhodesia, with Salisbury as capital

ledger.note: 1979: Zimbabwe Rhodesia is born. The state 'was a short-lived sovereign state that existed from 1 June 1979'; 'Zimbabwe Rhodesia was preceded by another state named the Republic of Rhodesia'; Abel Muzorewa of the UANC was appointed Prime Minister and Josiah Zion Gumede became president (Rhodesian Bush War page: 1 June 1979). The page gives no boundary: the land is the Rhodesia of the previous state.

1979: Zimbabwe Rhodesia returns to British rule. On 11 December 1979 'Zimbabwe Rhodesia shall cease to be an independent State and become part of Her Majesty's dominions'; the Lancaster House Agreement was 'signed on 21 December 1979' and the name 'formally reverted to Southern Rhodesia'. Independence as the Republic of Zimbabwe followed on 18 April 1980 (Bush War page: 'interim British rule ended and the country was internationally recognised as independent').

wars.name: Rhodesian Bush War
wars.outcome: Negotiated end: Lancaster House talks in December 1979, a ceasefire announced on 21 December 1979, elections under British supervision in early 1980 and independence on 18 April 1980.
wars.note: 'a civil conflict from July 1964 to December 1979'. ZANLA was 'present on a more or less permanent basis in over half the country' by the end; ZIPRA's bases were 'almost all' around Lusaka. Rhodesian raids into Mozambique (Operation Aztec, 30 May 1977; Operation Dingo, 23-25 November 1977) and Zambia (Westlands farm, October 1978) held no ground. No territory changed hands, so no zone is drawn.

certainty.note: The frontiers are the colonial and Rhodesian lines of the predecessor; neither page opened discusses them.

sources.title: Zimbabwe Rhodesia
sources.note: Existence 1 June 1979 to 18 April 1980, the 11 December 1979 law, Lancaster House (21 December 1979), the Muzorewa government; no area in the infobox.

sources.title: Rhodesian Bush War
sources.note: The war's dates (July 1964 to December 1979), the ceasefire of 21 December 1979, independence on 18 April 1980, cross-border raids.

notes: Cliopatria's Zimbabwe Rhodesia row runs 1979-1982 with the same 392,765 km2 shape as Rhodesia (1967-1978) and the Republic of Zimbabwe (from 1983): for the compiler this row is the stand-in for 1980-82. The end year is 1979 (the law of 11 December 1979), with a few months of British rule as Southern Rhodesia before the Republic of Zimbabwe on 18 April 1980; the Zimbabwe Rhodesia page's own infobox spans to 18 April 1980, so a reader of that page would put the end in 1980. The Rhodesian Bush War page says the country was renamed Zimbabwe-Rhodesia under the March 1978 agreement and dates the election to 24 April 1979, while the Zimbabwe Rhodesia page dates the presidential vote to 28 May 1979: neither moves a border. The republic-of-zimbabwe and rhodesia dossiers belong to other parts of af-08. No area figure for comparison was on either page (the infobox lists none).
